The '''family''' of the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]] was made up of [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirians]] [[Homeworld/Legends|from]] the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]]. [[Reproduction/Legends|Born]] to the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] [[Mother (title)/Legends|Mother]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]] and a [[Maul's father|nightbrother]], Maul was raised in the culture of the [[Nightbrothers/Legends|Nightbrothers]], along with his brothers [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] and [[Feral/Legends|Feral Opress]]. Talzin also had a [[Talzin's firstborn daughter|daughter]], who's birth nearly caused Talzin her life. Taken in by a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]], [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], as a child, Maul would not be reunited with his family until the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], in which he and Opress cut a path of destruction across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].

==History==
{{Quote|A brother? But all of my kin were ''killed''!"<br />"Not ''all'' of them. He lives in the Outer Rim, in exile.|Savage Opress learns of his long-lost brother, Darth Maul, from Mother Talzin|<ref name="Witches of the Mist" />}}
At some point, the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]] became pregnant with a [[Talzin's firstborn daughter|daughter]]. The [[Reproduction/Legends|birth]] of her daughter nearly caused her [[Death/Legends|death]], but she survived, an blessing which she attributed to the [[Spirit (Nightsisters)|Spirits]].<ref name="BOS">''[[Book of Sith: Secrets from the Dark Side]]''</ref> Sometime before [[54 BBY/Legends|54 BBY]],<ref name="MSbirthdate">[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Comic 6.35|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' Comic 6.35]] identifies Opress as the older brother to Darth Maul, whose birthdate is provided as [[54 BBY/Legends|54 BBY]] in [[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']].</ref> Talzin gave birth to a son, who was named [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]].<ref name="Savage&Feral">{{TCW|Witches of the Mist}} establishes that [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] is the blood brother of [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]], and {{TCW|Monster}} establishes that [[Feral/Legends|Feral]] is the blood brother of [[Feral/Legends|Feral]]. According to [[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']], [[Nightbrothers/Legends|Nightbrother]] fathers were killed after the [[Reproduction/Legends|birth]] of their son. Thus, three brothers could not be related through the same father, but instead from the same mother. According to [[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3|''Darth Maul—Son of Dathomir'' 3]], [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]] is the biological mother of Maul, and thus must also be the mother of Savage and Feral.</ref> In 54 BBY,<ref name="MSbirthdate" /> Talzin and a [[Maul's father|Nightbrother]] had a son named [[Darth Maul/Legends|Maul]].<ref name="SOD3" /> She also had another son named [[Feral/Legends|Feral]].<ref name="Savage&Feral" /> According to Talzin, during his visit to Dathomir, [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] had become associated with Talzin and planned to make her his apprentice, but took Maul instead and fleed the planet.<ref name="SOD3" /> Sidious himself, however, had actually encountered a Nightsister named [[Kycina]], who had claimed herself to be Maul's mother and begged him to take her infant away from Dathomir and out of Talzin's clutches.<ref name="Darth P" />

In [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]],<ref name="Monster Date">{{TCWdates|313}}</ref> Feral was killed by his own brother Savage after he was transformed into a [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] by Talzin with the intent to get revenge on [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]].<ref name="Monster" /> In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],<ref name="Lawless Date">{{FactFile2014|44|20 BBY 47-50|Maul on Mandalore}}</ref> Talzin's first son [[Savage Opress/Legends|Savage Opress]] was [[Death/Legends|killed]] by Darth Sidious.<ref name="TheLawless">{{TCW|The Lawless}}</ref> Talzin's last surviving son, Maul, was resurrected by [[Prophets of the Dark Side]].<ref name="Resurrection">{{Tales|9|Resurrection (comic story)}}</ref><ref name="Ron Marz Twitter">{{Twitter|ronmarz|status/1024143622424473600|Ron Marz|archivedate=20210308202224}}</ref> During a [[Duel on Kalakar Six|duel]] with [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]], Maul was killed again.<ref name="Resurrection" /> Then later during the reign of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], a [[Scientist/Legends|scientist]] named [[Drell Kahmf]] retrieved Maul's brain and spinal cord, put them in a specialized [[Bacta tank/Legends|bacta tank]], and hooked the bacta tank up to a [[Solid-state hologram|hologram]]. Later, the hologram was destroyed by [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="T17PM">{{Tales|17|Phantom Menaces}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In the novel ''[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|Darth Plagueis]]'' and short story "[[Restraint]],"<ref name="Restraint">{{StoryCite|story=Restraint|book=Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter}}</ref> [[Kycina]] is stated to be the mother of Darth Maul.<ref name="Darth P" /> However, the [[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3|third issue]] of [[Star Wars: Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir|''Darth Maul—Son of Dathomir'']] states that the mother of Maul is [[Mother (title)/Legends|Mother]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]].<ref name="SOD3" /> As ''Son of Dathomir'' is the most recent source, this article assumes the comic holds precedence.

A [[Maul's descendant|possible descendant]] or [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] of Maul was considered for the cancelled ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Battle of the Sith Lords]]'' by [[Red Fly Studio]]. The idea of the original Maul cloning himself or continuing his bloodline came as a solution for [[George Lucas]]' request to include [[Darth Talon]] in the plot despite her belonging to the ''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]'' era set more than one hundred years after Maul's life, with Lucas suggesting that through this way, Maul could still get to interact with Talon.<ref name="GI article2">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2014/04/09/art-from-the-darth-maul-game-you-39-ll-never-get-to-play.aspx|text=Art From The Darth Maul Game You'll Never Get To Play|author=Andrew Reiner|date=2014-04-09|work=[[Wikipedia:Game Informer|''Game Informer'']]|archivedate=20240223064541|nolive=1}}</ref> 

As part of the [[Wikipedia:GameStop|GameStop]] exclusive preorder of the [[2010]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II]]'', an exclusive avatar of a [[Canon|non-canon]] character named [[Maulkiller]] was given to players of the [[Wikipedia:Xbox 360|Xbox 360]] and [[Wikipedia:PlayStation 3|PlayStation 3]] versions. Maulkiller was created by Darth Vader using the [[DNA/Legends|genetic material]] of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Galen Marek]] and Darth Maul.<ref name="gamestop preorder">{{WebCite|url=http://www.gamestop.com/Catalog/ProductDetails.aspx?product_id=78039|text=Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II Collector's Edition - with Bonus!|author=Gamestop|format=Product preorder page|quote=Purchase Star Wars The Force Unleashed II and receive a GameStop exclusive in-game Maulkiller skin and silver saber crystal.|archivedate=20100823230451}}</ref>
